base:
Create ONE square, polished character design study for a tiny task-management app mascot, using the attached references. This is a static pose concept, not a screenshot or animation. Image 1 provides the exact existing character identity: an almost perfect, plump matte BLACK SPHERE with extremely restrained dark shading, two broad simple white line eyes, large round hands, a simple pale ivory pencil. Its current low side-hands pose is the problem to REDESIGN. Image 2 is a historical approved style sheet; ONLY its CENTER WRITING character is a pose/style inspiration, do not reproduce the other characters.

LOCK identity: a true circular body silhouette, no head/torso division, no ears, horns, feet, hair, clothing. Exactly TWO eye strokes total: broad, clean, essentially STRAIGHT white strokes with rounded ends, well separated across the face. No eyeballs, pupils, highlights, eyebrows, mouth, nose, cheeks, wrinkles, sweat, tears, zzz, motion marks or emoji decorations. Eye expression must feel gently diligent and cute, never angry, stern, tired or asleep. Keep inward eye angle mild (about 4–8 degrees), not a steep V. Give eyes a low and slightly sideward placement that reads as looking AT THE PENCIL TIP on a sphere, not flat stickers. White strokes conform subtly to face orientation but remain simple straight-looking strokes.

Hands must read as ROUND HANDS actively WRITING, not feet or two little spheres sitting on the ground. Use TWO large circular fingerless hands (each diameter around 28–32% of body diameter), absolutely NO thin connecting arms, wrists, fingers. Hold the hands in front of the LOWER FRONT FACE, HIGHER than the rejected side-feet pose; the passive hand is asymmetrically higher and a little behind. The near hand and the pale pencil form a clearly legible gripping silhouette. The pencil passes behind the round hand, with a visible upper shaft and a visible lower tip; do not draw fingers. Keep hands black/very dark charcoal, with a modest soft highlight to separate their circular foreground shapes from the black body; no hard white outline, no glossy plastic. Partial overlap is fine, the contours must be readable. Do not simply put both hands on opposite lower corners. Show only one short, tidy gray scribble directly at the pencil tip. No paper sheet, notebook, desk, floor shadow, background object, frame, watermark or logo.

Layout: one character centered on a clean warm-white background with generous margin, all hand and pencil parts fully visible, body occupies about 62% of image width. Very clean, understated, vector-friendly soft 2.5D rendering, smooth surfaces, zero fuzzy texture. All detail must survive a small app icon. Put one tiny unobtrusive letter label below the drawing as specified.

variants.prompt: A — FRONT HANDS, GENTLE DILIGENCE. Almost front-facing sphere. Bring the pencil hand onto the viewer-left lower front/cheek area, its center above the sphere's lower quarter; only a small part of its round outline protrudes beyond the left silhouette. Put the passive round hand on the lower RIGHT FRONT of the body, slightly higher and further in than the writing hand, with a clear foreground highlight, as a small companion stabilizing the work area. It must not hang below the body like a foot. Eyes sit comfortably far apart, oriented gently DOWN-LEFT toward the writing tip, with an almost horizontal, soft focused attitude. The pencil points diagonally down-right from the grip toward a small scribble just below-left of the sphere. Retain the compact cute silhouette of the historical center reference while improving hand/body separation. Text: "A".

B — SUBTLE THREE-QUARTER WRITER. Turn the facial features a modest 15–20 degrees toward viewer-left and pitch them slightly downward; the BODY outline stays perfectly circular. The eye nearer the viewer is slightly wider, the far eye slightly foreshortened, both broad straight rounded white strokes with generous spacing, calm concentration. Pose the large pencil hand forward-left in front of the lower face, raised enough to be clearly a hand; a tiny crescent of background can distinguish part of its outer edge. Place the other round hand on the RIGHT FRONT of the sphere but HIGHER and further back, visibly helping rather than standing on the ground. The two hands must be asymmetric in height and depth while retaining similar actual size, not a giant hand and tiny foot. Use mild charcoal shading to clarify overlapping planes. Pencil tip and both eyes aim toward the same lower-left writing spot. This pose should instantly read as absorbed in writing from a mild side view. Text: "B".

C — HEAD-DOWN, WORK CLOSE TO FACE. Keep a round sphere and express a modest forward bow with facial projection alone. Shift the two spacious straight rounded white eyes slightly lower on the front sphere, relaxed mild inward slopes, focusing on a writing spot DIRECTLY BELOW the middle of the face rather than far off to the side. Place the dominant large round pencil hand near the LOW FRONT CENTER-LEFT of the body, closer to the writing spot than in A; the pencil crosses down diagonally to a tiny scribble beneath the center. Raise the auxiliary round hand on the lower-right cheek, above the working hand, so the pose is unmistakably hands cooperating in front of the sphere, not paired feet. Give the hands subtle but legible charcoal tonal separation from the body. Convey quiet, adorable determination and a sense of leaning into work. No flattened bean body, no neck or extra appendages. Text: "C".

status: concepts awaiting user selection; no Rive or App mutation
